NRL Match Preview: Round 26 v Eels
The Sharks come into tomorrow's match with the Eels on the back of a vital win that saw the side click back into gear after back-to-back losses.
Both clubs' annually play for the Johnny Mannah Cup, in tribute to the champion prop who sadly passed away in 2013.
The Sharks have held the trophy since regaining it in last year’s 28-18 win over Parramatta at Magic Round in Brisbane.
Coach Craig Fitzgibbon said, "we’d like to pay our respects to the Mannah family for this game. It’s not lost on us.”
“Obviously, his brother Tim is a Parramatta legend and Johnny played for the Sharks. Shark #435 so it’s an important day for us too.”
With his side assured an NRL finals place this season, Fitzgibbon is set to become the first Cronulla coach to lead the club to 5 straight finals appearances.
But he’s made sure the Sharks are taking it game by game.
“Our fans are up and about and looking forward to the end of the year, but we’ve got a couple of challenges ahead before we get there so it’s good to have the fans onside and excited.”
“The Eels have shown some green shoots this year with a lot of improved players…so it’ll be a handful for us but we’re looking forward to the challenge,” he added.
The Sharks will also be motivated by more milestones.
The club's now second greatest try scorer of all-time, Ronaldo Mulitalo, will bring up his 150th NRL appearance for the club.
Cronulla have won 10/13 games since the winger returned from an ACL injury in round 11.
“I haven’t seen too many guys do more in the community, and give their time to people, on behalf of the Sharks than Ronnie," Fitzgibbon shared.
"His passion can come across as an antagonist. He just wants to win and sometimes that spills over but he’s just a player that you love to have in your side.
“His teammates adore him and other teams don’t like him, but that guy has got a big heart and we’re really lucky to have him that’s for sure."
The ever-impressive Jesse Colquhoun will bring up his 50th game for the club as well.
The 24-year-old was limited to just 11 games in his first three seasons due to injury, but his next 38 have flown by since returning in round 9 last year.
"Jesse came back from a broken foot, (another) broken foot and then an ACL, so the start to Jesse’s career has been littered with challenge and turbulence but he’s shown… what sort of player he’s going to be," Fitzgibbon continued.
“We’re really happy that we’ve re-signed him for a long period of time because we think he’s the future in that position (lock).”
Cronulla has won three of the past four games against Parramatta, all three by 10 points or less, but at CommBank Stadium the Sharks have won one of three against the Eels.
Cronulla has won 12 of 13 games this season when leading at halftime, and won two of nine when trailing at the break, including last week’s come from behind victory over the Titans.
The Sharks have won 11 of 14 games when scoring the first try, but won three of eight when conceding first, and have conceded the last try in the past six games.
Nicho Hynes needs seven points to pass Luke Covell (948) for third most points for Cronulla and is also chasing his 100th NRL career win in what will be his 147th game.

August 28 th 2026, 8:57pm , By: Ben Bridge
Sunday afternoon NRL at CommBank Stadium gives us the "hold your nose" bet of Round 26 for Eels vs Sharks .
Cronulla is clearly the better team. They are fifth, still have a top 4 opportunity and enter after a 30-22 win over Gold Coast. Parramatta sit near the bottom and are already thinking about 2027. And yet, I am taking Eels +6.5.
The reason is partly venue and partly matchup. Parramatta have won three of their past four at CommBank Stadium, with the only loss in that stretch coming by six points against Penrith. Cronulla, meanwhile, looked noticeably less fluent last weekend without Braydon Trindall and needed a strong second half to get past the Titans.
The Sharks remain without Trindall, leaving Nicho Hynes and Niwhai Puru in the halves. Braden Uele returns on the bench. Parramatta have Dylan Walker named after a wrist issue and largely retain the side that started strongly against the Dolphins last week.
This is not a bet built on believing Parramatta are suddenly good. It is a bet against asking Cronulla to win comfortably when their attack is still adjusting.

Parramatta’s 34-16 loss to the Dolphins was a genuine tale of two halves. The Eels started brilliantly and raced to a 10-0 lead midway through the opening half before the Dolphins gradually took control and ran away with the game.
That opening period is important for this handicap. Parramatta looked dangerous when they were able to play through Mitchell Moses and attack with early ball. Their problem was sustaining the effort once the Dolphins’ powerful back five started winning field position.
The Eels’ second half defence eventually cracked, but they at least demonstrated they still have enough attacking threat to trouble finals teams.
CommBank Stadium has also quietly become a much better venue for them recently. Their home form is one of the few reasons for optimism in a difficult season, and Penrith are the only side to have beaten them there across their past four appearances, by just six.

The penultimate round of the 2026 NRL regular season features a bounty of high-profile encounter – headlined by Canterbury’s must-win clash against Penrith and a top-four showdown between the Roosters and Dolphins.

The Storm have lost four of their last five but followed up a 42-20 thrashing of Manly in Perth with a 22-14 home loss to heavyweight Penrith last week.

items.title: Surgery likely to rule Sam Walker out for season in brutal Roosters blow
items.snippet: The Queensland Origin No.7 has had his worst fears confirmed on Sunday morning after suffering an ankle injury against the ...
items.body_excerpt:
Roosters star Sam Walker is set to undergo ankle surgery that will almost certainly end his season.
Scan results revealed that Walker suffered a high-grade syndesmosis strain in Saturday’s 26-12 loss to the Dolphins and requires a corrective operation to his ankle, potentially as early as Monday.
Walker was sent for scans on Saturday night after he was collected in an awkward collision with Dolphins back-rower Kulikefu Finefeuiaki, with follow-up consultations on Sunday morning confirming the club’s worst fears.
Veteran recruit Daly Cherry-Evans and utility Hugo Savala shape as a ready-made halves pairing in Walker’s absence.
Multiple Roosters sources have confirmed Walker will undergo surgery, but the club is unwilling to rule a line through him completely given the typical 6-8 week recovery timeframe his operation entails.
With the NRL grand final 35 days away, a miracle comeback won’t be completely dismissed given Cherry-Evans has made a five-week return from ankle surgery previously. Former captain and assistant coach Boyd Cordner’s recovery from a badly broken ankle to play in the 2013 decider is also the stuff of legend at Roosters HQ.
Daly Cherry-Evans will now take charge of the Roosters attack. Getty Images
In any case though, the injury is an especially cruel blow for Walker, who has been in career-best form after suffering a season-ending ACL rupture leading into the finals two years ago.
Walker’s sidelining comes after he and the club parked contract talks – with Walker taking a lead role in that decision – when the Roosters most recent five-year, $5 million offer fell short of what his camp believes he can get on the open market when the NRL’s salary cap rises.
Both parties had agreed to wait until the Tricolours campaign ended before resuming negotiations. Walker’s preference has always been to ink a long-term extension at the club rather than go to market on November 1.
This masthead reported two weeks ago that the Walker camp was seeking around $250,000-$300,000 more per season than the Roosters had originally offered.
Sam Walker was in distress as he left the field on Saturday night. Getty Images
On the paddock, Trent Robinson’s side will take on arch-rivals South Sydney this Friday night, needing a win to guarantee a top-four finish.
Walker’s absence is a telling blow, and comes alongside doubts around whether Victor Radley (concussion) will play or be kept on ice for another week leading into the finals.
Radley suffered his eighth concussion or failed HIA in five years against the Wests Tigers last Sunday and is now required to gain clearance from an independent doctor to play again.
He is due to complete the NRL’s mandatory 11-day stand-down concussion protocols a day before kick-off against the Rabbitohs, but the Roosters have always taken an ultra-conservative approach with players returning from head knocks as well, and no call has yet been made on the English international’s return.
Veteran winger Daniel Tupou (shoulder) is firming to return against Souths, while rugby-union-bound back-rower Angus Crichton (broken foot) will be back either this Friday or in week one of the finals.
Back-to-back losses to the Tigers and Dolphins over the past two rounds have dropped Trent Robinson’s side from first to fourth on the ladder.
Losing to the Rabbitohs would open the door for Cronulla to pinch fourth place if they can finish the regular season with wins over Parramatta and Melbourne.
Meanwhile, scans will confirm if Jarome Luai has played his last game for the Wests Tigers.
Luai failed to finish the game against the Cowboys on Saturday night, with club officials confirming he suffered a lower leg injury.
Coach Benji Marshall was not asked about Luai after the loss, and made it clear he was unimpressed with some of the refereeing decisions, which he labelled “outrageous”.
Luai announced earlier this year he would be joining the PNG Chiefs for the start of the 2028 season , with the club later agreeing to cut him

There were initial concerns that Walker had been caught in a hip drop tackle, but the replay showed Finefeuiaki was already on the ground.

Hugo Savala moved into the halves upon Walker’s departure, but was unable to steer the side to a comeback alongside Daly Cherry-Evans .
The hosts were provided every opportunity to get back into the match at Allianz Stadium with the Dolphins down to 11 men at one stage.
Tom Flegler had been sent to the sin bin in the 60th minute when it was 26-6 for repeat infringements. His teammate Morgan Knowles was then given the same punishment seven minutes later for a hip drop.
Salesi Foketi crossed for a try to make it 26-12 with the two-man advantage, but substitute winger Tommy Talau bombed a couple of try-scoring opportunities late in the piece as the Dolphins cemented themselves as title contenders.
But the big story is the Roosters, who will now be forced to contend for their first premiership in seven years without their marquee playmaker.
Speaking on Nine’s Sunday Footy Show , Slater admitted that the pressure was now on a couple of Walker’s experienced teammates to fill the void.
“[This will have a] huge impact. He’s one of their go-to players, he’s instrumental in all the good things they do, he is so creative and he’s unpredictable,” Slater said.
“You need your best players on the field at this time of the year. Two weeks ago, the Roosters had won eight in a row and they were flying – how times can change.
Daly Cherry-Evans will now take charge of the Roosters attack. Getty Images
“It’s a tough situation for the Roosters at the moment, because how do they replace him? The two people who really need to stand up for me now are Victor Radley, he plays that ball-playing first receiver role in the middle of the field, he will take pressure off Daly Cherry-Evans, who is the other guy.
“He’s one of the greatest kickers in the game’s history and he will need to stand up. He only does 50 per cent of the kicks – he will have to do 100 per cent now.”
Roosters hooker Reece Robson also left the field in the final nine seconds.
They will meet local rivals South Sydney in round 27 and may need to win that game in order to keep the Sharks out of the top-four.

items.snippet: Luai’s Tigers farewell at risk as Cowboys lock in top eight spot    Nine.com.au
items.body_excerpt:
Tigers fans could have seen Jarome Luai in the club’s jersey for the last time after he hobbled off the field late in a 20-10 loss to the Cowboys .
With five minutes left, Luai was swung around in a one-on-one tackle from Braidon Burns and stayed down before eventually playing the ball.
Tigers trainer Brett Hodgson attends to Jarome Luai. Getty Images
The Tigers half then left the field at Queensland Country Bank Stadium on a night where multiple players continued to slip over.
“Could this be his final game as a Tiger?” caller Brenton Speed said on Nine.
The Tigers have one match left this season, against Penrith next Sunday, before Luai joins the Eels.
Luai was also placed on report for high contact on Tom Chester.
The Cowboys’ win means they are now locked into the top eight with one match in hand but Billy Slater wasn’t convinced by their showing in Townsville.
Read more

“I thought they were very underwhelming, I wasn’t impressed with their performance at all,” he said on Nine.
“The only positive that came out of it was they got two points and booked a semi-final berth. They’ve got a fortnight now to get their game on ... if they play like this in September they won’t be going on for very long.”
The Cowboys were on the board first when Chester ran through a gaping hole created on the Tigers edge.
Four minutes later the Tigers hit back when Jeral Skelton won the race to a Jarome Luai grubber.
Then in the 22nd minute it looked like the Tigers had pulled off a sensational play when Luai ran 90 metres after a Cowboys error.
However, the replay showed Api Koroisau had hit the ball out of Thomas Mikaele’s hands which led to a penalty and two points for the Cowboys.
Tom Chester. Getty Images
The Tigers managed to get points back when Junior Tupou scored to make it 10-8 at half-time.
North Queensland came out of the sheds the better side, scoring three unanswered tries through Heilum Luki, Jaxon Purdue and Chester, to seal victory.
Jeremiah Nanai was an injury concern throughout the match for the Cowboys, appearing to struggle with a knee problem. However, he did play 68 minutes.
Next week the Cowboys play the Raiders on Saturday.

As it happened: Knights strike back; Roosters undefeated, Titans go eight straight
The Titans kicked off Saturday's NRLW action by taking down the Raiders 26-20 in an entertaining contest at Cbus Super Stadium.
The two sides were hard to split for much of the first half until the Lauren Brown show really kicked off, orchestrating three tries in seven minutes leading into half-time to put the Titans in front 18-6.
The Titans marched on in the second half and the lead blew out to 26-6, but the Raiders were not going to let it end there, scoring three late tries to close the gap, with Mackenzie Wiki finishing with a hat-trick including a remarkable team try after the full-time siren.
It was the eight straight win for the Titans and solidifies them in second position on the ladder.
In the second game, the Roosters made it nine in a row against a Sharks outfit enduring a horror injury run. They were unfortunately struck again in the game with forward Rhiannon Byers suffering a knee injury in their 36-8 loss.
The final instalment of our Saturday triple took us to Townsville where the Cowboys were looking to continue a late charge that had seen them win three of their past four matches to climb from last on the ladder to ninth.
However, the visiting Newcastle proved far too strong, overpowering the home side with a dominant 40-6 win, putting them back on track after a string of losses had seem them in danger of missing the finals for the first time since their inaugural season in 2021.
